attribution.note: Marcus's own words, the opening line of his own Substack post.

semantics.note: The claim is an unhedged statement about the present state of AI. Dropping the second clause, about reshaping the world on that premise, is acceptable because it is a separate claim.

contract.note: The plain reading (substantially short of broadly human-level competence) is ordinary and fair. But Marcus never defines AGI or 'close', so whether the claim holds depends on a proximity threshold the contract itself requires to be independently justified. None was supplied.

evidence.note: March 2025 ARC-AGI-2 launch, within the period. Large human-AI gap on unfamiliar reasoning tasks, but it covers one capability family and gives no measure of how close AGI is.
August 2025 ARC-AGI-3 preview, within the period. Humans beat the games while AI agents struggled. Only three preview games and preliminary human baselines; no threshold for proximity.
October 2025 preprint, within the period. Gold-medal astronomy theory scores alongside consistent reasoning weaknesses. Mixed capability evidence that does not settle proximity either way.
2024 framework paper, before the target period. Conceptual background only; it gives no state of capability for 2025.

reviews.rationale: The evidence shows real gaps on fluid reasoning and interactive learning (e1, e2) and strong but uneven performance elsewhere (e3). The contract asks for broad comparable evaluations plus an independently justified measure of proximity. The packet admits no source provides one, and the evidence covers only selected capability families. A gap alone does not show AGI is distant, so the packet does not settle whether AI was 'not close'.
